assumptions: Evaluation universe per genome = true pairs + every pair emitted by any executed arm, on labelled proteins only; the universe (and hence ECE/Brier) depends on which arms are compared and is identical for all arms of a genome.
A pair in the universe that an arm did not emit has score 0 (omission is not rewarded).

Closed world: a universe pair without a label is counted false, although labels are incomplete, so precision is a lower bound. This is a convention, not a guarantee of equal bias: arms that call more specific, novel or less-studied functions are penalised more than arms that call well-annotated ones, and correct but unlabelled calls are invisible. Compare arms with different specificity profiles conditionally on label completeness.
Proteins without any label of the scored kind are not evaluated; global Fmax picks its threshold on the evaluated labels.
